corpusSummary: This corpus comprises 2026-era social-science studies on large language models spanning behavior, human–AI interaction, education, health, policy, and research methods. It highlights tensions between AI capabilities and embodied knowledge, issues of anthropomorphism, bias, and misinformation, and showcases LLMs as tools for analysis, design, and governance—prompting attention to trust, safety, ethics, and equitable deployment across domains.

themes.name: LLM behavior, bias, and social dynamics
themes.description: A body of work investigates anthropomorphism, hallucinations, misinformation susceptibility, polarization, and emergent social dynamics of AI agents, emphasizing calibration and governance needs.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, adoption, and literacy
themes.description: Research across education, health, and everyday use examines trust formation, adoption barriers, social influence, empathy, embodiment, and AI literacy with implications for well-being and learning.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological innovation
themes.description: Papers explore using LLMs for data analysis, codebook construction, policy study, climate sentiment, urban planning, and discourse analysis, while addressing validation, transparency, and ethical concerns.

themes.name: AI in education and learning ecosystems
themes.description: Studies address AI-enabled tutoring, scaffolding, assessment, literacy, and teacher adoption, along with student engagement, anxiety, and the broader implications for pedagogy and curriculum.

emergingKeywords: AI as research tool and methodology
